# Jose Maria Perez-Macias, PhD - Academic & Research Portfolio

> Biomedical & Telecommunications Engineer, Healthcare Technology Researcher, and Technical Leader. Specializing in unobtrusive sleep monitoring, contactless physiological sensors, biomedical signal processing, ballistocardiography (BCG), and 3D spatial audio. Currently affiliated with Aalto University; doctoral degree completed at Tampere University, Finland.

## Current Research & Scientific Focus

1. **Wearable Sensors & Sensor Fusion (Smartwatches, Wrist EMG + PPG)**:
   - Investigating multi-modal sensor fusion combining wrist Surface Electromyography (EMG) and Photoplethysmography (PPG) to dramatically enhance heart rate estimation accuracy during motion artifacts in smartwatches (*IEEE Sensors Journal*, 2022).

2. **Ballistocardiography (BCG) & Contactless Heart Pulse Demodulation**:
   - Isolating and demodulating continuous heartbeat and arterial pulse signals from unobtrusive bed mattress sensors (Emfit) using non-negative tensor factorization and spectral demodulation (*CinC*, 2022).
   - Generating position-independent pulse signals that correlate with reference ECG and PPG for non-invasive cardiovascular and sleep monitoring.

3. **Unobtrusive Sleep Monitoring & Contactless Diagnostics**:
   - Pioneering algorithms for non-contact electro-mechanical film (Emfit) bed transducers to track sleep stages, cardiac cycles, and respiratory dynamics without body-worn sensors.

4. **Snoring Classification & Acoustic Source Separation**:
   - Machine learning pipelines utilizing Support Vector Machines (SVM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) to detect and classify snoring events (*IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics*, *Physiological Measurement*).

5. **Clinical Respiratory Effort & Pediatric Ventilation**:
   - Developing automated detection algorithms for upper airway resistance, prolonged partial obstructions, and abnormal ventilation patterns in pediatric and adult sleep monitoring (*Child Neurology Open*, *Springer IFMBE*).

## Doctoral Dissertation

- **Title**: *Methods for Snoring and Heart Pulse Detection Using Unobtrusive Mattress Sensor*
- **Author**: Jose Maria Perez-Macias
- **Degree**: Doctoral Dissertation, Tampere University, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences and Engineering, June 2025
- **Permanent URN**: [http://urn.fi/URN:ISBN:978-952-03-2953-7](http://urn.fi/URN:ISBN:978-952-03-2953-7)
- **Institutional Repository**: [Tampere University Trepo (Handle: 10024/227620)](https://trepo.tuni.fi/handle/10024/227620)
- **ISBN**: 978-952-03-2952-0 (print), 978-952-03-2953-7 (pdf)
- **Summary**: Investigates signal processing architectures for extracting vital physiological parameters from contactless Emfit bed mattress sensors. Establishes novel algorithms for position-independent heart pulse demodulation and machine learning models for accurate snoring event detection.

## Computational Modeling & Simulation Projects

- **COMSOL Simulation of Action Potential Propagation (FitzHugh-Nagumo Model)**:
  - Educational computational study simulating nerve axon excitation and action potential propagation in COMSOL Multiphysics using the FitzHugh-Nagumo reaction-diffusion PDE system coupled with extracellular electrostatics. Includes governing equations, 3D tetrahedral mesh design, threshold/refractory parameter sweeps, and animated simulation videos.
  - URL: https://jperezmacias.github.io/biomedical-projects/comsol-neuron/

## Audio & Signal Processing Projects

- **Acoustic Source Localization & Vehicle Tracking (Advanced Audio Processing, Tampere University)**:
  - Educational project and tutorial examining acoustic beamforming with circular microphone arrays (miniDSP UMA-8, 8 channels) and Steered Response Power with Phase Transform (SRP-PHAT) algorithms to track moving vehicles in road traffic.
  - URL: https://jperezmacias.github.io/projects_audio/sound-localization/
  - Code: https://github.com/jperezmacias/project_advanced_audio

- **3D Spatial Audio & Csound DSP (2004 Course Project)**:
  - Undergraduate student project on 3D audio, Head-Related Transfer Functions (HRTF), and digital sound synthesis opcodes in Csound from 2004 (Universidad de Valladolid). Maintained as an online legacy educational reference.
